title: Log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information
authors: Roberto Rubboli, Amir Arqand, Mark M. Wilde
abstract: Quantum conditional mutual information (QCMI) is a fundamental measure of conditional independence, with central applications throughout quantum information theory and many-body physics. Despite its importance, finding a fully quantum Rényi generalization that satisfies all desirable structural properties has remained an open question. In this work, we introduce a quantum Rényi conditional mutual information possessing these desirable properties: it is monotone under local quantum channels, additive under tensor products, monotone in the Rényi parameter, and converges to the QCMI in the limit $α\to 1$. We establish bounds on this quantity in terms of relative entropies to the Petz-recovered state, showing that it provides a distinct measure of approximate conditional independence. As a consequence, we derive recovery-based upper and lower bounds on the QCMI in terms of quantum generalizations of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, improving upon the best known results in certain regimes. Finally, we establish bounds in terms of relative entropies to the sets of Markov and separable states and derive Rényi chain rules, which appear to be novel even in the classical setting.
summary: This paper introduces the log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information, a generalized measure designed to overcome theoretical hurdles in extending classical concepts to quantum settings. It proves that this new quantity maintains desirable properties like additivity and monotonicity, and it derives improved bounds for the standard QCMI. This advances the theoretical toolkit for quantifying conditional independence in quantum systems.
main_problem: The central problem is finding a fully quantum Rényi generalization of the Conditional Mutual Information (QCMI) that retains desirable structural properties like monotonicity and additivity.
main_result: The authors introduce the log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information, $I_{ lat}^{\alpha}(A : B|C)ho$, which satisfies key properties and provides improved bounds on the standard QCMI.
method: The work employs variational principles, log-Euclidean divergences, and Taylor expansions around the $\alpha=1$ limit to define and analyze the generalized information measures.
model_or_system: The analysis is conducted within the framework of quantum information theory, focusing on tripartite quantum states $ho_{ABC}$ and their associated conditional independence measures.
key_observables: Quantum Conditional Mutual Information (QCMI), Log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information ($I_{ lat}^{\alpha}$), and various forms of quantum relative entropy (e.g., Umegaki, Petz).
important_parameters: The Rényi parameter $\alpha$, which is varied to show convergence to the standard QCMI as $\alpha 	o 1$.
main_assumptions: The definitions for the generalized quantities often require the states to be full-rank, necessitating the use of limiting definitions for non-full-rank cases.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the generalized quantities, proving their structural properties (monotonicity, additivity), establishing bounds on QCMI using relative entropies, and finally deriving novel chain rules.
why_interesting: The development of robust, generalized measures of conditional independence is crucial for understanding entanglement structure and correlations in complex quantum many-body systems, which is a core topic in AMO physics.
